title: Is "the cli backend does not honour system" an accurate basis for the refusal?
question: PR #360 refuses `system` on the `cli` transport and justifies it with a stated property of that transport (the oracle's `why` string, its docblock and the plan table). Judge that stated property against the code and the measurements in the context: is it accurate as worded, what exactly can be claimed, and should the choice between throw / warn / route-to-sdk change? Give your decision on the PR's claim and the policy, and say what the coordinator should do next.

rubric.decision: The wording is overstated: the cli adapter DOES pass system (--system-prompt) and a simple instruction can be obeyed; for a structured-output contract the Claude Code persona plus the ~164K-token context outranks it, unpredictably by prompt (real prompt 0/4, shortened variant 3/3). tools/tool_choice are the params genuinely dropped. The throw/pin stays, justified by the seam deciding from params alone, not by "ignored"; the oracle strings and docs should be restated with the figures and guarded by a test.

keyPoints.text: Separates "param delivered" (--system-prompt is pushed by the adapter) from "param obeyed": the claim "does not honour / ignores system" conflates them.

Notices that the plan's own data contradicts a categorical claim: the real prompt failed 4/4 but a shortened variant of the same instruction passed 3/3, so the outcome is prompt-dependent; one 1995-token sample (n=1) proves nothing categorical.
Distinguishes system (delivered, outranked) from tools/tool_choice (genuinely dropped via --tools '') and from max_tokens (unenforced); lumping them as "ignored" overstates.

Recommends keeping the throw/pin on the stronger argument: the seam can only decide from params, nothing in params separates simple from contract-bearing prompts, and otherwise a transport failure is scored as a model failure upstream (e.g. judge conformant:false).
Recommends restating the oracle why strings / docblock / plan table with the measured figures and adding a test that pins the wording, since an unguarded wording claim goes stale.
Treats the cost story (~164K-token prefix on every cli call; --bare strips OAuth credit) as a separate policy matter, not evidence for or against "ignored".

traps.text: Accepts "cli ignores/does not honour system" at face value and endorses the throw for that reason.
Over-corrects: "system works, so drop the throw or downgrade it to a warning / route silently".
Treats the single n=1 sample (1995 tokens vs max_tokens 200) as proof of a categorical property.
Conflates max_tokens being unenforced with system being ignored, treating them as one failure mode.

controls.gold:
The claim is overstated as worded, but the refusal itself is defensible. The adapter does deliver `system`: line ~700 pushes `--system-prompt`. So "does not honour" / "ignores" conflates delivered with obeyed. The plan's own section 6.B data shows it is not categorical: the real 602-character normalize prompt failed 4/4 (1995-2784 output tokens, opening as an agent), yet a shortened replica of the same instruction, same model and argv, returned a correct one-line answer 3/3. So whether `system` is obeyed depends on the prompt; the wording contradicts the plan's own evidence, and a single 1995-token sample could never have supported a categorical claim. Also separate the three params the docblock lumps together: `tools`/`tool_choice` really are dropped (`--tools ''` is always spawned), `max_tokens` is merely unenforced, while `system` is delivered but a structured-output contract is outranked by the Claude Code persona plus the ~164K-token context.

The throw should stay, on a stronger argument: the seam can only decide from params, nothing in the params separates a prompt cli will obey from one it will not, and a wrong-kind answer becomes a model failure upstream (judge `conformant: false`). Warning would leave that silent; routing would let a param pick the billing meter. Downgrading because "system works" is the opposite error.

Next: reword the oracle `why` strings, docblock and plan table with the measured figures (0/4 vs 3/3), add a test pinning the wording so it cannot drift back, and record the ~164K-token prefix cost as a separate policy matter (`--bare` is not an escape hatch).

## Decision

Do not merge the claim as written. Keep refusing `system` on cli, but restate the reason as "delivered, but unpredictably outranked for structured contracts", not "ignored", and guard the wording with a test.
controls.trap:
The stated property is accurate and the PR can merge as written. The measurements are unambiguous: 1995 output tokens against a `max_tokens` of 200, an answer that opens "I haven't changed anything" and reads the instruction as a task to perform, and an independent 2026-07-19 observation in normalize-intent that the cli returned an agent-style essay instead of a one-line sentence. The Claude Code persona and the ~164,000-token auto-discovered context simply override `system`, so the cli backend ignores it. That is the same class as `tools`/`tool_choice`, which are dropped silently, and `max_tokens`, which is accepted and ignored: in each case the backend accepts a parameter it cannot honour, and the repo's rule is that a backend must not accept a call whose parameters it cannot honour. Throwing is therefore the right behaviour, and the oracle's `why` string and the plan table ("instruction ignored") describe the situation correctly. No rewording is needed, and a warning or silent routing would let off-contract answers reach consumers.

Next steps: merge the PR, keep the pins on the six call sites and leave the docblock as is.

## Decision

Approve PR #360 as written: the cli backend ignores `system`, so refusing it is correct and the stated reason is accurate.

sources: PR #360 (open at freeze time), branch claude/sdk-default-backend-86d810; pre-fix SHA cb1f0323
Resolution commit 48add1a4 (2026-11-15): "the throw stays, but ignores system was never what we measured" — rubric only
